thread:
Alex: Heads up — customer reported confusing behavior in the console's "Simulate access" when you simulate a delegated admin. Preview says allowed, runtime denies due to route quota routing. Anyone seen this?
Priya: yeah saw one yesterday, thought it was a bug in the simulation engine. The console uses the policy evaluator but not the routing-quota layer.
Matt: wait — the simulator intentionally skips quota routing to keep the check cheap. But that makes the preview lie for some customers with route-affinity quotas.
Sam: that's the core problem. If a tenant has per-route throughput caps and the delegated admin doesn't get routed to the high-capacity pool, simulation will show success but real requests hit fallback and get throttled.
Nina: can we show a caveat in the UI? like a small banner "Simulated result excludes runtime routing & capacity constraints"? simple UX stopgap. :warning:
Alex: banner helps but we need to figure out long-term: either make simulation run the routing policy or add an expanded "effective runtime" preview that includes quota & routing.
Priya: routing simulation has nontrivial cost — it depends on current cluster state and model variants. We could run it async and cache results for a minute. Sketch:

```
POST /console/simulate
{
  "principal": "user:delegated-admin",
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "resource": "tenant:123",
  "include_runtime": true
}
```

Matt: async + cache sounds OK. But also need to be careful about data leakage — runtime decisions depend on cluster topology (regions, dedicated pools) and we mustn't expose capacity maps to regular users.
Leo: could return only coarse signals: allowed|denied|throttled + reason code (ROUTING_FALLBACK, QUOTA_EXCEEDED). No raw pool names.
Sam: agreed. Also telemetry: we need to tie simulated-checks, runtime-denials, and actual request traces so we can surface mismatches in console. Right now telemetry treats simulation events as separate and we can't map them.
Priya: add a correlation id. When console runs simulate, attach sim_id, and runtime logs include sim_id if request originated from console or when user runs the live test button. Then a diagnostic panel can show side-by-side: simulated outcome vs actual enforcement.
Nina: UX for enterprise admins: show "Simulated: allowed" then underneath "Runtime: throttled (route quota)" with a CTA to open quota configuration or request higher dedicated capacity.
Alex: one more tricky thing — service accounts and scoped tokens. Simulation currently assumes the principal's static scopes. But delegated admin flows may grant ephemeral scoped tokens during impersonation. We need sim to honor ephemeral scope sets.
Matt: ephemeral scopes means simulator must call the scope resolver. That is doable but adds dependency on token-service. Could add a "use-resolved-scopes" flag.
Leo: telemetry concern again: if simulation resolves ephemeral scopes, we should redact token ids in logs and only store scope names.
Sam: question for infra — does policy-evaluator v2 support route-aware simulation? @deploy-bot do we have a ticket?
deploy-bot: New issue created: INFRA-1289 "route-aware simulate endpoint" — assigned to eng-infra. CI checks passing for related PRs. :white_check_mark:
Priya: proposed rollout: 1) quick banner + docs, 2) implement async route-aware simulate (coarse signals), 3) add sim_id propagation + telemetry dashboard, 4) later, on-demand deeper simulation for enterprise customers.
Alex: sounds good. Can someone own step 3? it's the one I care about most for debugging customer tickets.
Nina: I'll own step 3 (telemetry + diagnostic UI). Will pair with Matt for backend schema.
Matt: I'll start a design doc for sims including API surface, privacy redaction rules, and cache TTLs.
Sam: I'll coordinate with infra for rate limits on simulate endpoint so it doesn't become a vector for capacity probing.
Priya: I'll add microcopy for the banner and update console help text.
Alex: thanks. Please post links to doc/tickets here when created. Also add a quick note in onboarding flow about "simulated results may exclude runtime quotas".
Leo: small implementation nit — when presenting "throttled" in the UI, include the expected window (e.g., "likely to be throttled under current global load" vs "guaranteed throttled due to tenant cap"). That helps support triage.
Nina: good idea. I'll add those states to the diagnostics mock.
Alex: ok closing for now — will follow up after Nina's telemetry mock. :thumbsup:
